verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents a token-authenticated API that it says can do 'anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI', with API keys acting like a user with Owner permissions by default. It also publishes an official MCP server, so a dashboard-free agent loop is plausible. However, the specific acknowledge, escalate and resolve operations are only implied by the UI-parity claim, and the OpenAPI probe found no machine-readable spec at the standard paths. missing for 10: explicit documentation of alert-acknowledge, escalate and incident-resolve endpoints or MCP tools, a discoverable OpenAPI spec, hands-on or independent corroboration of an end-to-end agent workflow.
